claims.head: Something has to give
claims.body: The Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. Our lean: the Rangers’ chance quality wins out.
claims.call: The Rangers’ chances are more dangerous than the league average (a 6.3% chance of scoring on the average shot) against the Kings.

claims.head: The Rangers will send Schneider and Šmits at Perry
claims.call: The Rangers’ P3 (Schneider and Šmits) spends at least 34% of its 5-on-5 time against the Kings’ fourth line.
claims.body: At home, the Rangers keep sending Schneider and Šmits out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Mike Sullivan has been picking a defense pair for opponents’ fourth lines. Tonight the Kings’ fourth line is Wright, Helenius and Perry.

NYR.head: The Rangers start a half-step ahead
NYR.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage, and the Kings may be without Byfield. Still, it’s close: the Kings can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

LAK.head: The Kings start a half-step behind
LAK.body: Los Angeles has been out-chancing opponents lately, but the Rangers have home-ice advantage, and the Kings may be without Byfield. The Kings can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Who’s in net for the Rangers?
paras: The Rangers are 7-4-1. The Kings have won two in a row.

It’s strength against strength: the Rangers are near the top of the league for chance quality, but the Kings are one of the best at preventing dangerous shots. At home, Mike Sullivan likes to pick matchups, so watch who goes out against the Kings’ fourth line.
